title.zh: 卷三十八 蜀書八 許麋孫簡伊秦傳
title.en: Volume 38: Book of Shu 8 - Biographies of Xu, Mi, Sun, Jian, Yi, and Qin
title.raw: 卷三十八 蜀書八 許麋孫簡伊秦傳 Volume 38: Book of Shu 8 - Biographies of Xu, Mi, Sun, Jian, Yi, and Qin

sentences.zh: 許靖字文休，汝南平輿人。

translations.literal: Xu Jing, courtesy name Wenxiu, was a man of Pingyu in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jing, styled Wenxiu, came from Pingyu in Runan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少與從弟劭俱知名，並有人倫臧否之稱，而私情不協。

translations.literal: In youth he and his younger cousin Shao were both famous, and together they had a reputation for judging men and ranking character, but in private feeling they were not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he and his cousin Xu Shao rose to fame together, and both were celebrated for sizing up men of the age, yet the two never got along in private.

sentences.zh: 劭為郡功曹，排擯靖不得齒敘，以馬磨自給。

translations.literal: Shao became merit assessor of the commandery, excluded Jing so that he could not be ranked in order, and Jing supported himself by grinding grain with a horse mill.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao served as the commandery’s merit assessor, he shut Xu Jing out of official placement altogether, and Xu was reduced to earning a living at a horse-driven mill.

sentences.zh: 颍川劉翊為汝南太守，乃舉靖計吏，察孝廉，除尚書郎，典選舉。

translations.literal: Liu Yi of Yingchuan became grand warden of Runan, thereupon recommended Jing as clerk on the annual accounts, investigated him as filial and incorrupt, appointed him gentleman of the masters of writing, and put him in charge of selections.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi of Yingchuan, as grand warden of Runan, nominated Xu Jing as accounts clerk, then recommended him on the filial-and-incorrupt roll; Xu was appointed gentleman of the Secretariat and given charge of personnel appointments.

sentences.zh: 靈帝崩，董卓秉政，以漢陽周毖為吏部尚書，與靖共謀議，進退天下之士，沙汰穢濁，顯拔幽滯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ling died, Dong Zhuo seized government, appointed Zhou Bi of Hanyang as director of the Ministry of Personnel, and with Jing together deliberated, advancing and retiring the gentlemen of the realm, washing away the foul and turbid, and manifestly elevating the secluded and blocked.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ling’s death, Dong Zhuo took power. He named Zhou Bi of Hanyang director of personnel and had him work with Xu Jing to decide promotions and dismissals across the empire—purging the corrupt and raising men who had long languished in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 進用颍川荀爽、韓融、陳紀等為公、卿、郡守，拜尚書韓馥為冀州牧，侍中劉岱為兗州剌史，颍川張咨為南陽太守，陳留孔伷為豫州剌史，東郡張邈為陳留太守，而遷靖巴郡太守，不就，補御史中丞。

translations.literal: They advanced and employed Xun Shuang, Han Rong, Chen Ji, and others of Yingchuan as dukes, ministers, and grand wardens; invested Masters of Writing Han Fu as shepherd of Ji province, Palace Attendant Liu Dai as inspector of Yan province, Zhang Zi of Yingchuan as grand warden of Nanyang, Kong Zhou of Chenliu as inspector of Yu province, Zhang Miao of Dong commandery as grand warden of Chenliu; and transferred Jing to be grand warden of Ba commandery, but he did not take up the post, and was instead supplemented as palace assistant secretary.
translations.idiomatic: They brought in men such as Xun Shuang, Han Rong, and Chen Ji of Yingchuan to fill the highest civil posts and commandery governorships; Han Fu was made shepherd of Ji, Liu Dai inspector of Yan, Zhang Zi grand warden of Nanyang, Kong Zhou inspector of Yu, and Zhang Miao grand warden of Chenliu. Xu Jing was slated for Ba commandery, but he declined the post and was appointed assistant secretary of the imperial censorate instead.

sentences.zh: 馥等到官，各舉兵還向京都，欲以誅卓。

translations.literal: When Fu and the others reached their posts, each raised troops and turned back toward the capital, intending thereby to execute Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Once Han Fu and his colleagues reached their assignments, they each mobilized forces and marched on the capital, aiming to destroy Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓怒毖曰︰「諸君言當拔用善士，卓從諸君計，不欲違天下人心。

translations.literal: Zhuo angrily said to Bi: "You gentlemen said one ought to promote and employ good gentlemen; Zhuo followed your gentlemen's plan and did not wish to go against the hearts of men under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo rounded on Zhou Bi in fury: "You insisted we elevate worthy men. I followed your counsel because I would not set myself against the will of the realm.

sentences.zh: 而諸君所用人，至官之日，還來相圖。

translations.literal: Yet as for the men your gentlemen employed, on the day they reached office, they returned to plot against me.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the very men you placed in office turned their armies against me the moment they took up their posts.

sentences.zh: 卓何用查負！

translations.literal: What use has Zhuo for being betrayed!
translations.idiomatic: What have I done to deserve such treachery in return?

sentences.zh: 」叱毖令出，于外斬之。

translations.literal: " He shouted at Bi ordering him out, and outside beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Zhou Bi hustled outside and executed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 靖從兄陳相玚，又與伷合規，靖懼誅，奔伷。

translations.literal: Jing's elder cousin Yang, chancellor of Chen, again with Zhou joined in plotting; Jing feared execution and fled to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jing’s cousin Xu Yang, who was chancellor of Chen, was also in league with Kong Zhou’s designs; fearing he would be put to death, Xu Jing fled to Kong Zhou’s camp.

sentences.zh: 〈蜀記雲：靖後自表曰：「黨賊求生，情所不忍；

translations.literal: The Shu Ji states: Later Jing himself in a memorial said: "To cling to rebels to seek life, in feeling is what I cannot bear;
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Ji records that Xu Jing later explained in a memorial: "To side with rebels merely to save my skin was more than conscience would allow;

sentences.zh: 守官自危，死不成義。

translations.literal: to guard office and endanger oneself, to die and not complete righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: to cling to an empty title while peril closed in would have been a death that accomplished no duty worth the name.

sentences.zh: 竊念古人當難詭常，權以濟其道。」〉

translations.literal: I privately thought that the ancients, facing difficulty, altered the constant, and by expediency aided their way."
translations.idiomatic: I recalled how the ancients, in extremity, bent the usual rules and used timely shifts of course to preserve what truly mattered."

sentences.zh: 伷卒，依揚州剌史陳祎。

translations.literal: When Zhou died, he relied on Chen Yi, inspector of Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: After Kong Zhou died, Xu Jing took refuge with Chen Yi, the inspector of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 祎死，吳郡都尉許貢、會稽太守王朗素與靖有舊，故往保焉。

translations.literal: When Yi died, Commandant of Wu Commandery Xu Gong and Grand Warden of Kuaiji Wang Lang, who from old had ties with Jing, therefore went to protect there.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yi died, Wu’s commandant Xu Gong and Kuaiji’s grand warden Wang Lang—both old acquaintances—offered Xu Jing shelter.

sentences.zh: 靖收恤親裡，經紀振贍，出于仁濃。

translations.literal: Jing gathered and comforted kin and neighborhood, managed and relieved and supported, coming from thick benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jing gathered his kinsmen and neighbors, organized relief, and kept them fed—acts born of deep human kindness.

sentences.zh: 孫策東渡江，皆走交州以避其難，靖身坐崖邊，先載附從，疏親悉發，乃從后去，當時見者莫不嘆息。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce crossed east over the river, all fled to Jiaozhou to avoid his disaster; Jing himself sat on the cliff edge, first loading followers and attendants, distant kin all dispatched, then afterward went himself; those who saw at the time none did not sigh.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce crossed the Yangzi, everyone bolted for Jiaozhou to escape the storm. Xu Jing sat on the bluff until the last boat: he sent off followers and distant kin first and only then embarked himself, and all who watched were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 既至交阯，交阯太守士燮濃加敬待。

translations.literal: Having reached Jiaozhi, Grand Warden of Jiaozhi Shi Xie thickly added respectful treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached Jiaozhi, Grand Warden Shi Xie received him with exceptional courtesy and respect.

sentences.zh: 陳國袁徽以寄寓交州，徽與尚書令荀彧書曰︰「許文休英才偉士，智略足以計事。

translations.literal: Yuan Hui of Chen state, because lodging in Jiaozhou, Hui in a letter to Masters of Writing Director Xun Yu said: "Xu Wenxiu is a heroic talent and great gentleman; wisdom and strategy are sufficient to plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hui of Chen, then living in exile in Jiaozhou, wrote to Xun Yu, director of the Secretariat: "Xu Wenxiu is a man of outstanding ability; his judgment is more than equal to the weightiest counsel.

sentences.zh: 自流宕已來，與群士相隨，每有患急，常先人后已，與九族中外同其飢寒流。

translations.literal: From the time of drifting exile, following with the crowd of gentlemen, whenever there was peril and urgency, he always put others before himself, and with the nine degrees of kin inside and outside shared their hunger, cold, and wandering.
translations.idiomatic: Since he was cast adrift, he has traveled with every sort of scholar; whenever danger struck, he put others first and took the hardship on himself, sharing hunger and cold with kinsmen near and far alike.

sentences.zh: 其紀綱同類，仁恕惻隱，皆有效事，不能複一二陳之耳。

translations.literal: As for his ordering his kind, benevolence, forbearance, and commiseration, all have deeds that can be verified; it is not possible again to set them forth one by one in the ear.
translations.idiomatic: The way he leads those around him, his kindness, tolerance, and compassion—all of it can be documented in concrete acts too numerous to recount one by one.

sentences.zh: 」巨鹿張翔

translations.literal: " Julu Zhang Xiang
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Xiang of Julu

sentences.zh: 〈《萬機論》云：翔字元鳯。〉

translations.literal: The Wan Ji Lun states: Xiang's courtesy name was Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Wan Ji Lun gives Zhang Xiang’s courtesy name as Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 銜王命使交部，乘勢募靖，欲與誓要，靖拒而不許。

translations.literal: Bearing the king's command he was envoy to the Jiao region, riding the momentum recruited Jing, wishing to swear covenant with him; Jing refused and did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with an imperial mission to the south, Zhang Xiang tried to use his leverage to recruit Xu Jing into a binding pledge, but Xu Jing steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 靖與曹公書曰︰

translations.literal: Jing in a letter to Lord Cao said:
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jing wrote to Lord Cao as follows:

sentences.zh: 世路戎夷，禍亂遂合，駑怯偷生，自竄蠻貊，成闊十年，吉凶禮廢，昔在會稽，得所貽書，辭旨款密，久要不忘。

translations.literal: The world's roads are armored barbarians; disaster and chaos then joined; timid and cowardly, stealing life, I myself fled into Man and Mo; fully ten years wide, auspicious and inauspicious rites abandoned; formerly in Kuaiji I obtained the letter you sent; the wording was sincere and intimate, long covenant not forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: The age has turned to arms and turmoil; calamities crowd upon one another. Craven and afraid, I clung to life and fled into the southern wilds, where a full decade has slipped away and the rites of weal and woe have all broken down. Back in Kuaiji I received the letter you sent: its tone was warm and earnest, and I have never forgotten the bond it spoke of.

sentences.zh: 迫于袁術方命圮族，扇動群逆，津涂四塞，雖縣心北風，欲行靡由。

translations.literal: Pressed by Yuan Shu, who was ordering the destruction of the clan, fanning and moving the crowd of rebels, fords and roads blocked on four sides; although my heart hung on the north wind, wishing to go there was no way.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu was tearing the realm apart and inciting every rebel band; every route was sealed. Though my heart was fixed on the north, I could find no road that would take me there.

sentences.zh: 正禮師退，術兵前進，會稽傾覆，景興失據，三江五湖，皆為虜庭。

translations.literal: Zhengli's army retreated, Shu's troops advanced forward, Kuaiji overturned, Jingxing lost footing, the three rivers and five lakes, all became barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao’s forces fell back while Yuan Shu’s host pressed forward; Kuaiji collapsed, Wang Lang lost his footing, and the lands between the great rivers and lakes became enemy-held ground.

sentences.zh: 臨時困厄，無所控告，便與袁沛、鄧子孝等浮涉滄海，南至交州。

translations.literal: Facing the moment's hardship and peril, having nowhere to appeal, then with Yuan Pei, Deng Zixiao, and others floated and crossed the deep sea, southward arriving at Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped and with no one to turn to, I put to sea with Yuan Pei, Deng Zixiao, and the rest, crossed the ocean, and made my way south to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 經歷東甌、閩、越之國，行經萬里，不見漢地，漂薄風波，絕糧茹草，飢殍荐臻，死者大半。

translations.literal: Passing through the states of Eastern Ou, Min, and Yue, traveling ten thousand li, not seeing Han land, drifting thin in wind and waves, cutting grain and eating grass, hunger and corpses repeatedly arriving, the dead more than half.
translations.idiomatic: We passed through Eastern Ou, Min, and Yue—ten thousand li without a glimpse of heartland Han soil—buffeted by wind and waves, starving until we chewed wild plants; famine and death came in waves, and more than half our company perished.

sentences.zh: 既濟南海，與領守兒孝德相見，知足下忠義奮發，整飭元戎，西迎大駕，巡省中岳。

translations.literal: Having crossed the South Sea, met acting warden Er Xiaode, knew your foot's loyalty and righteousness stirred up, put in order the great army, westward welcomed the great chariot, toured and inspected the central marchmount.
translations.idiomatic: After we crossed the southern sea I met your deputy Er Xiaode and learned how you have roused yourself in loyal duty, marshaled the host, marched west to welcome the emperor, and toured the sacred central peak.

sentences.zh: 承此休問，且悲且憙，即與袁沛及徐元賢複共嚴裝，欲北上荊州。

translations.literal: Receiving this good news, both sad and glad, immediately with Yuan Pei and Xu Yuanxian again together strictly equipped, wished to go north to Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: Your welcome word left me both grief-stricken and glad; at once Yuan Pei, Xu Yuanxian, and I readied ourselves again for the road north to Jing province.

sentences.zh: 會蒼梧諸縣夷、越蜂起，州府傾覆，道路阻絕，元賢被害，老弱並殺。

translations.literal: It happened that in the various counties of Cangwu the Yi and Yue swarmed up, prefecture and headquarters overturned, roads blocked and cut off, Yuanxian was harmed and killed, old and weak together killed.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Yi and Yue of Cangwu rose like a swarm; the regional government collapsed, every road was cut, Xu Yuanxian was murdered, and old and young were slaughtered together.

sentences.zh: 靖尋循渚崖五千餘里，複遇疾癘，伯母隕命，並及群從，自諸妻子，一時略盡。

translations.literal: Jing then followed the islets and cliffs more than five thousand li, again encountered pestilence; his paternal aunt lost her life, together reaching the crowd of cousins, down to wives and children, in one moment largely exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: I skirted the shoals and headlands for another five thousand li, only to be struck by epidemic: my aunt died, then cousin after cousin, until wives and children alike were swept away almost to a person.

sentences.zh: 複相扶侍，前到此郡，計為兵害及病亡者，十遺一二。

translations.literal: Again mutually supporting and attending, forward arriving at this commandery, reckoning those harmed by arms and those who died of illness, ten retained one or two.
translations.idiomatic: Those of us who could still lean on one another limped into this commandery; of all who had fallen to weapons or sickness, perhaps one or two in ten were left.

sentences.zh: 生民之艱，辛苦之基，豈可具陳哉﹗

translations.literal: The hardship of the living people, the foundation of bitter toil, how can it be fully set forth!
translations.idiomatic: The bitterness common folk endure, the sheer grind of staying alive—how could I possibly describe it all?

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以為孔子稱「賢者避世，其次避地」，蓋貴其識見安危，去就得所也。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi considers: Confucius called "the worthy avoid the age, next they avoid the place," probably valuing their perceiving safety and danger, going and staying obtaining what is right.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks: Confucius said the wise withdraw from a degenerate age and, failing that, from a dangerous place—because he prized the judgment that knows when to stay and when to flee.

sentences.zh: 許靖羈客會稽，閭閻之士，孫策之來，於靖何為？

translations.literal: Xu Jing was a sojourning guest in Kuaiji, a man of the lanes and gates; Sun Ce's coming, for Jing what was there to do?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jing was a private gentleman lodging in Kuaiji when Sun Ce arrived—what real threat did that pose to him personally?

sentences.zh: 而乃泛萬里之海，入疫癘之鄉，致使尊弱塗炭，百罹備經，可謂自貽矣。

translations.literal: Yet then floated the sea of ten thousand li, entered the land of pestilence, causing honored and weak to be smeared and charred, hundred calamities all experienced, can be called self-bringing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he chose to cross ten thousand li of ocean and plunge into plague-ridden country, dragging elders and children through every imaginable horror—he brought that suffering on himself.

sentences.zh: 謀臣若斯，難以言智。

translations.literal: A planning minister like this, difficult to call wise.
translations.idiomatic: A strategist who behaves so can hardly be called wise.

sentences.zh: 孰若安時處順，端拱吳、越，與張昭、張紘之儔同保元吉者哉？〉

translations.literal: How compared to peacefully abiding the times and dwelling in compliance, reverently folding hands in Wu and Yue, with Zhang Zhao, Zhang Hong's ilk together preserving primordial auspiciousness?"
translations.idiomatic: How much better to have waited out the turmoil in Wu and Yue with hands quietly folded, keeping company with men like Zhang Zhao and Zhang Hong and sharing in their good fortune?"

sentences.zh: 懼卒顛仆，永為亡虜，憂瘁慘慘，忘寢與食。

translations.literal: Fearing in the end to fall over, forever becoming a fleeing captive, anxious and worn miserable miserable, forgetting sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: I feared I might collapse and end my days a fugitive slave; grief wore me so thin I forgot to eat or sleep.

sentences.zh: 欲附奉朝貢使，自獲濟通，歸死闕庭，而荊州水陸無津，交部驛使斷絕。

translations.literal: Wishing to attach to the court tribute envoy, himself obtain passage through, return to die at the palace gate, but Jing province water and land had no ford, Jiao region post riders were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped to join an imperial courier, win a clear road home, and die within sight of the throne—yet Jing province offered no crossing by land or water, and the post roads through the south were dead.

sentences.zh: 欲上益州，複有峻防，故官長吏，一不得入。

translations.literal: Wishing to go up to Yi province, again there were steep defenses, former officials senior clerks, not one obtaining entry.
translations.idiomatic: I tried the route into Yi province, but barriers stood everywhere: not even former officials could get through.

sentences.zh: 前令交阯太守士威彥，深相分托于益州兄弟，又靖亦自與書，辛苦懇惻，而複寂寞，未有報應。

translations.literal: The former order Grand Warden of Jiaozhi Shi Weiyan, deeply mutually entrusted to Yi province brothers, again Jing also himself wrote letters, bitter earnest sincere, yet again silent, not having response.
translations.idiomatic: Your predecessor as Jiaozhi’s grand warden, Shi Xie, had urged the Liu brothers in Yi on my behalf, and I myself poured my heart into letter after letter—yet the silence never broke; no word came back.

sentences.zh: 雖仰瞻光靈，延頸企踵，何由假翼自致哉？

translations.literal: Although gazing up at the bright numen, stretching neck standing on tiptoe, by what means borrow wings and arrive oneself?
translations.idiomatic: I lift my eyes toward your radiance and stand on tiptoe straining to hear—yet without wings how am I to reach you?

sentences.zh: 知聖主允明，顯授足下專征之任，凡諸逆節，多所誅討，想力競者一心，順從者同規矣。

translations.literal: Knowing the sagely lord is truly enlightened, clearly has entrusted you with exclusive campaign authority; as for all rebellious violations, many have been executed and attacked; I suppose those who resisted with force are now of one mind, and those who complied share the same standard.
translations.idiomatic: I know the sage Son of Heaven trusts your judgment and has given you full power to chastise rebellion; most of the traitors have already been cut down, while former foes must now stand as one and every man who yields follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 又張子雲昔在京師，志匡王室，今雖臨荒域，不得參與本朝，亦國家之藩鎮，足下之外援也。

translations.literal: Further, Zhang Ziyun formerly was in the capital, minded to restore the royal house; now although he faces wild borderlands and cannot participate in this court, he is also a screen town of the state, your external aid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ziyun once served in the capital with his heart set on shoring up the house of Han; though duty now keeps him on a distant frontier far from court, he remains a pillar of the empire and an ally beyond your borders.

sentences.zh: 〈子雲名津，南陽人，為交州刺史。

translations.literal: Ziyun's name was Jin; he was a man of Nanyang and served as inspector of Jiao province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ziyun’s personal name was Jin; he was from Nanyang and held the post of inspector of Jiao province.

sentences.zh: 見《吳志》。

translations.literal: See the Records of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: See the "Book of Wu" in the Sanguozhi.

sentences.zh: 《漢書霍光傳》曰：「光出都肄郎羽林，道上稱警蹕。

translations.literal: The Han Shu biography of Huo Guang states: "When Guang left the capital to drill the gentlemen of the Feathered Forest, on the road they proclaimed warning and halting."
translations.idiomatic: The Han Shu biography of Huo Guang records: "When Guang left the capital to review the Gentlemen of the Feathered Forest at drill, the procession cleared the road with the imperial warning and halting signals."

sentences.zh: 」未詳虎賁所出也。〉

translations.literal: " It is not yet clear where the passage about the tiger halberdiers comes from."
translations.idiomatic: The origin of the remark about the imperial halberdiers (hǔbēn) remains unclear."

sentences.zh: 若荊、楚平和，王澤南至，足下忽有聲命于子雲，勤見保屬，令得假途由荊州出，不然，當複相紹介于益州兄弟，使相納受。

translations.literal: If Jing and Chu are peaceful and harmonious, royal grace south reaches, you suddenly have a voiced command to Ziyun, earnestly see him protected and attached, order that he be allowed to borrow a road and exit through Jing province; if not so, then again mutually introduce through Yi province brothers, causing them mutually to receive.
translations.idiomatic: Should peace return to Jing and Chu and the emperor’s favor reach the south, a single word from you to Ziyun—asking him to shelter me and let me borrow passage out through Jing—would suffice. Failing that, you might broker an introduction to the Liu brothers in Yi so that they would take me in.

sentences.zh: 倘天假其年，人緩其禍，得歸死國家，解逋逃之負，泯驅九泉，將複何恨﹗若時有險易，事有利鈍，人命無常，隕沒不達者，則永銜罪責，入于裔土矣。

translations.literal: If Heaven lends him years and men slacken their disasters, obtaining to return and die for the state, resolving the burden of flight, extinguishing driven to the nine springs, what again would be regret! If times have peril and ease, affairs have sharp and dull, human life has no constancy, those who fall and do not reach, then forever bear guilt responsibility, enter into border soil.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven grants me years and men stay their hands long enough for me to go home and die in the emperor’s service, my debt as a fugitive would be cleared and I could descend to the shades without regret. But if fortune turns, affairs go awry, and I perish on the road without ever arriving, I shall bear shame to my grave and end my days in this barbarous borderland.

sentences.zh: 昔營邱翼周，杖鉞專征，博陸佐漢，虎賁警蹕。

translations.literal: In old times Yingqiu aided Zhou, grasped axe exclusive campaign; Bolu assisted Han, tiger guards warning halts.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Yingqiu aided the Zhou with axe and charter of independent command; the Marquis of Bolu served the Han with imperial halberdiers clearing his road—such was the majesty of those ministers.

sentences.zh: 今日足下扶危持傾，為國柱石，秉師望之任，兼霍光之重，五侯九伯，製御在手，自古及今，人臣之尊未有及足下者也。

translations.literal: Today you support peril and hold the leaning, act as pillar stone for the state, grasp the duty of Taigong Wang, combine Huo Guang's weight, the five marquises and nine chiefs, control in hand; from antiquity to now, the honor of a subject has not reached one who matches your feet.
translations.idiomatic: Today you steady a tottering throne and serve as the state’s mainstay: you wield the authority of a Taigong Wang and match the power Huo Guang commanded; the great lords of the realm bend to your rein. Never in history has a subject stood so high.

sentences.zh: 夫爵高者憂深，祿濃者責重。

translations.literal: As for one whose rank is high, worry is deep; emolument thick, responsibility is heavy.
translations.idiomatic: High rank brings heavy cares, and rich stipends lay a crushing burden of duty.

sentences.zh: 足下據爵高之任，當責重之地，言出于口，即為賞罰，意之所存，便為禍福。

translations.literal: You occupy a rank-high post, stand in a responsibility-heavy place; words coming out of the mouth immediately become reward and punishment; what the mind harbors immediately becomes disaster and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: You hold an exalted office with commensurate responsibility: whatever leaves your lips becomes reward or punishment, and whatever you intend becomes weal or woe for others.

sentences.zh: 行之得道，即社稷用寧；

translations.literal: If in acting one obtains the Way, then the altars of soil and grain thereby are tranquil;
translations.idiomatic: Act in accord with the Way, and the altars of state will know peace;

sentences.zh: 行之失道，即四方散亂。

translations.literal: if in acting one loses the Way, then the four quarters scatter in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: stray from it, and the four quarters will fly apart in disorder.

sentences.zh: 國家安危，在于足下；

translations.literal: The state's safety and danger lie in you;
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the dynasty rests with you;

sentences.zh: 百姓之命，縣于執事。

translations.literal: the hundred surnames' lives hang on the executive.
translations.idiomatic: and the lives of the common people hang on your administration.

sentences.zh: 自華及夷，颙颙注望。

translations.literal: From Hua reaching Yi, look up look up pour gaze.
translations.idiomatic: From the central plains to the border peoples, all lift their eyes to you in hope.

sentences.zh: 足下任此，豈可不遠覽載籍廢興之由，榮辱之機，棄忘舊惡，寬和群司，審量五材，為官擇人？

translations.literal: You bearing this, how can you not broadly view in records the causes of ruin and rise, the triggers of glory and shame, cast aside and forget old evils, broadly harmonize the host of offices, carefully measure the five materials, for offices select men?
translations.idiomatic: Bearing such a charge, can you afford not to study how realms rise and fall, what brings honor or ruin, lay old grudges aside, treat your colleagues with generosity, weigh each man’s true talents, and match the right person to every post?

sentences.zh: 苟得其人，雖讎必舉；

translations.literal: If one obtains the right man, although an enemy one must raise him;
translations.idiomatic: When you find the right man, promote him even if he was once your foe;

sentences.zh: 苟其非人，雖親不授。

translations.literal: if it is not the right man, although kin one does not entrust.
translations.idiomatic: when he is unfit, withhold office even from your own kin.

sentences.zh: 以寧社稷，以濟下民，事立功成，則系音于管弦，勒勛于金石，愿君勉之﹗為國自重，為民自愛。

translations.literal: By this pacify the altars of soil and grain, by this aid the lower people; when affairs are established and merit completed, then tie sound on strings and pipes, carve merit on metal and stone; I wish you strive! For the state weigh yourself, for the people love yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Thus you will steady the altars of state and bring relief to the people; when the work is done and merit won, your name will be sung to music and graven in bronze and stone. I urge you to press on—guard your person for the sake of the realm and of every soul who depends on you.

sentences.zh: 翔恨靖之不自納，搜索靖所寄書疏，盡投之于水。

translations.literal: Xiang resented Jing's not accepting himself, searched Jing's sent letters and memorials, all threw them into water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiang, furious that Xu Jing would not join him, seized every letter Xu had sent and drowned the lot in a river.

sentences.zh: 後劉璋遂使使招靖，靖來入蜀。

translations.literal: Afterward Liu Zhang then sent envoys to summon Jing, and Jing came and entered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Zhang sent messengers to invite Xu Jing, and Xu came west into Shu.

sentences.zh: 璋以靖為巴郡、廣漢太守。

translations.literal: Zhang appointed Jing as grand warden of Ba commandery and Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang appointed him grand warden of Ba commandery and of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 南陽宋仲子于荊州與蜀郡太守王商書曰︰「文休倜儻瑰瑋，有當世之具，足下當以為指南。」

translations.literal: Song Zhongzi of Nanyang, being in Jing province, in a letter to Grand Warden of Shu commandery Wang Shang said: "Wenxiu is free and easy, splendid and rare, has the capacity of the present age; you should take him as compass needle."
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhongzi of Nanyang, writing from Jing province to Wang Shang, grand warden of Shu commandery, said: "Xu Wenxiu is a man of striking talent and rare breadth—he has everything needed to meet the demands of our times. You should treat him as your guiding star."

sentences.zh: 〈益州耆舊傳曰：商字文表，廣漢人，以才學稱，聲問著於州里。

translations.literal: The Yizhou Qijiu Zhuan states: Shang's courtesy name was Wenbiao; he was a man of Guanghan, famed for talent and learning, reputation heard manifest in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Traditions of the Elders of Yi province records that Wang Shang, styled Wenbiao, was a native of Guanghan celebrated for literary and scholarly ability, whose name resounded through the region.

sentences.zh: 劉璋辟為治中從事。

translations.literal: Liu Zhang summoned him as administrative clerk on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang appointed him administrative clerk on his staff.

sentences.zh: 是時王塗隔絕，州之牧伯猶七國之諸侯也，而璋懦弱多疑，不能黨信大臣。

translations.literal: At this time the royal path was cut off; the province's shepherds and elders were like the feudal lords of the Seven States, yet Zhang was weak, timid, and much suspicious, and could not unite and trust great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial authority no longer reached the provinces, and each regional lord acted like a Warring States prince; Liu Zhang was timid and suspicious by nature and could not bring himself to trust his senior officials fully.

sentences.zh: 商奏記諫璋，璋頗感悟。

translations.literal: Shang presented a memorial remonstrating Zhang; Zhang somewhat was moved to realize.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang submitted a formal remonstrance, and Liu Zhang took the lesson to heart.

sentences.zh: 初，韓遂與馬騰作亂關中，數與璋父焉交通信，至騰子超復與璋相聞，有連蜀之意。

translations.literal: At first, Han Sui and Ma Teng made rebellion in Guanzhong, repeatedly exchanged letters with Zhang's father Yan; reaching Teng's son Chao again communicated with Zhang, having intention to link Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Han Sui and Ma Teng stirred up trouble in Guanzhong, they had exchanged letters more than once with Liu Zhang’s father, Liu Yan; later Ma Chao renewed contact with Liu Zhang, hinting at an alliance with Yi province.

sentences.zh: 商謂璋曰：「超勇而不仁，見得不思義，不可以為脣齒。

translations.literal: Shang said to Zhang: "Chao is brave but not benevolent; seeing gain he does not think of righteousness; cannot be taken as lips and teeth."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang warned Liu Zhang: "Ma Chao is fierce but lacks humaneness; where he sees profit he forgets duty. He would make a treacherous neighbor—no true shield for your teeth and lips."

sentences.zh: 老子曰：『國之利器，不可以示人。

translations.literal: Laozi said: 'The state's sharp weapon cannot be shown to others.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi said, ‘The sharp weapons of a state must not be displayed to others.’

sentences.zh: 』今之益部，士美民豐，寶物所出，斯乃狡夫所欲傾覆，超等所以西望也。

translations.literal: ' Now the Yi region, scholars beautiful, people abundant, treasures produced, this is what cunning men desire to overturn; it is why Chao and the like gaze west.
translations.idiomatic: Yi province today boasts fine gentlemen and a prosperous populace and yields treasures that tempt every schemer—precisely why Ma Chao and his ilk keep looking westward.

sentences.zh: 若引而近之，則由養虎，將自遺患矣。

translations.literal: If you draw him near, then it is like raising a tiger; you will bring disaster on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: To invite him close would be to rear a tiger in your own courtyard—you would be asking for calamity."

sentences.zh: 」璋從其言，乃拒絕之。

translations.literal: " Zhang followed his words, then refused him.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Zhang heeded the advice and turned Ma Chao away.

sentences.zh: 荊州牧劉表及儒者宋忠咸聞其名，遺書與商敘致殷勤。

translations.literal: Jing province shepherd Liu Biao and the scholar Song Zhong both heard his name, sent letters to Shang expressing earnest cordiality.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao, shepherd of Jing province, and the scholar Song Zhong had both heard of Wang Shang and wrote him letters of warm regard.

sentences.zh: 許靖號為臧否，至蜀，見商而稱之曰：「設使商生於華夏，雖王景興無以加也。

translations.literal: Xu Jing was titled judge of character; arriving in Shu, seeing Shang he praised him saying: "Suppose Shang had been born in Huaxia, even Wang Jingxing could not surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jing, famed as a judge of men, came to Shu and, on meeting Wang Shang, declared: "Had this man been reared in the heartland of the empire, even Wang Lang could not have surpassed him."

sentences.zh: 」璋以商為蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: " Zhang appointed Shang as grand warden of Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Zhang thereupon made Wang Shang grand warden of Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 成都禽堅有至孝之行，商表其墓，追贈孝廉。

translations.literal: In Chengdu Qin Jian had utmost filial conduct; Shang memorialized his tomb, posthumously invested filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chengdu commoner Qin Jian was celebrated for supreme filial piety, Wang Shang petitioned at his tomb and had him honored posthumously on the filial-and-incorrupt roll.

sentences.zh: 又與嚴君平、李弘立祠作銘，以旌先賢。

translations.literal: Further with Yan Junping and Li Hong erected shrines and made inscriptions, thereby to signal former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He also founded shrines with inscriptions for Yan Junping and Li Hong to honor past sages of the region.

sentences.zh: 脩學廣農，百姓便之。

translations.literal: He repaired learning and broadened agriculture; the hundred surnames found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted schools and expanded farming, to the great benefit of the people.

sentences.zh: 在郡十載，卒於官，許靖代之。〉

translations.literal: In the commandery ten years, died in office; Xu Jing replaced him."
translations.idiomatic: He served ten years in the commandery and died in office; Xu Jing succeeded him."

sentences.zh: 建安十六年，轉在蜀郡。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an, he transferred to be in Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian’an 16 he was transferred to Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈山陽公載記曰：建安十七年，漢立皇子熙為濟陰王，懿為山陽王，敦為東海王。

translations.literal: The Shanyang Gong Zaiji states: In the seventeenth year of Jian'an, Han established the imperial son Xi as prince of Jiyin, Yi as prince of Shanyang, Dun as prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanyang Gong ji notes that in Jian’an 17 the Han court invested the imperial sons—Liu Xi as prince of Jiyin, Liu Yi as prince of Shanyang, and Liu Dun as prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 靖聞之曰：「『將欲歙之，必固張之；

translations.literal: Jing hearing it said: "'If one wishes to shrink it, one must first firmly expand it;
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jing heard the news he said, "‘If you would close your hand on something, you must first open it wide;

sentences.zh: 將欲取之，必固與之』。

translations.literal: if one wishes to take it, one must first firmly give it.'"
translations.idiomatic: if you would seize it, you must first let it go.’"

sentences.zh: 其孟德之謂乎！」〉

translations.literal: Is this not what is meant of Mengde!"
translations.idiomatic: Surely that describes Cao Mengde’s design!"

sentences.zh: 十九年，先主克蜀，以靖為左將軍長史，先主為漢中王，靖為太傅。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the First Lord conquered Shu, appointed Jing as chief clerk to the General of the Left; when the First Lord became Prince of Hanzhong, Jing became Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Liu Bei took Shu and named Xu Jing chief clerk to the general of the left; when Liu Bei became prince of Hanzhong, Xu Jing was made grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 及即尊號，策靖曰︰「聯獲奉洪業，君臨萬國，夙宵惶惶，懼不能綏。

translations.literal: When he ascended the honored title, in the edict to Jing said: "I have obtained to receive the great enterprise, lord over ten thousand states, morning and night anxious anxious, fearing unable to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: When he assumed the imperial title he addressed Xu Jing in the investiture rescript: "I have inherited the great charge and now rule the myriad regions; night and day I tremble, lest I fail to bring peace."

sentences.zh: 百姓不親，五品不遜，汝作司徒，其敬敷五教，在寬。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames are not close; the five grades are not compliant; you shall act as Minister of Education; respectfully spread the five teachings; reside in leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The people are not yet knit together, and the five relationships lack harmony. You shall serve as minister of education: reverently spread the five moral teachings and anchor your rule in clemency."

sentences.zh: 君其勖哉﹗秉德無怠，稱聯意焉。」

translations.literal: You, strive! Uphold virtue without slackness, match my meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Strive in this office! Uphold virtue without slackening, and you will fulfill my intent."

sentences.zh: 芳為南郡太守，與關羽共事，而私好攜貳，叛迎孫權，羽因覆敗。

translations.literal: Fang was grand warden of Nan commandery, together with Guan Yu served in office, but in private liking carried two minds, rebelled welcoming Sun Quan, Yu thereby overturned and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Fang was grand warden of Nan commandery and served alongside Guan Yu, yet he secretly harbored divided loyalties, defected to welcome Sun Quan, and Guan Yu’s armies were destroyed in consequence.

sentences.zh: 竺面縛請罪，先主慰諭以兄弟罪不相及，崇待如初。

translations.literal: Zhu with face bound requested punishment; the First Lord comforted and instructed with brothers' crimes not reaching one another, honored treatment as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Zhu came bound hand and foot to beg forgiveness. Liu Bei consoled him, saying a brother’s guilt does not extend to the kin, and treated him with the same esteem as before.

sentences.zh: 竺慚恚發病，歲餘卒。

translations.literal: Zhu ashamed and resentful fell ill, after more than a year died.
translations.idiomatic: Shame and bitterness wore him down until he fell ill, and a little over a year later he died.

sentences.zh: 子威，官至虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: The son Wei, office reached Colonel of the Rapid as Tigers among Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mi Wei rose to the rank of colonel of the Rapid as Tigers among Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 威子照，虎騎監。

translations.literal: Wei's son Zhao, supervisor of Tiger Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Wei’s son Mi Zhao served as supervisor of the Tiger Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 自竺至照，皆便弓馬，善射御雲。

translations.literal: From Zhu down to Zhao, all were convenient with bow and horse, good at archery and charioteering, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: From Mi Zhu through Mi Zhao the line produced men handy with bow and horse and skilled in archery and riding, or so tradition has it.

sentences.zh: 孫乾字公佑，北海人也。

translations.literal: Sun Qian, courtesy name Gongyou, was a man of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian, styled Gongyou, was a native of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 先主領徐州，辟為從事，

translations.literal: When the First Lord held Xuzhou, he was summoned as clerk on the staff,
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei took charge of Xuzhou, Sun Qian was recruited as a clerk on his staff,

sentences.zh: 〈鄭玄傳雲：玄薦乾於州。

translations.literal: The biography of Zheng Xuan states: Xuan recommended Qian to the province.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan’s biography records that Zheng recommended Sun Qian to the provincial authorities.

sentences.zh: 乾被辟命，玄所舉也。〉

translations.literal: Qian received the summoning appointment; it was Xuan who recommended him."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian’s appointment came through Zheng Xuan’s nomination."

sentences.zh: 后隨從周旋。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed in turning and circling.
translations.idiomatic: After that he followed Liu Bei through every campaign and crisis.

sentences.zh: 先主之背曹公，遣乾自結袁紹，將適荊州，乾又與麋竺俱使劉表，皆如意指。

translations.literal: When the First Lord turned his back on Lord Cao, he sent Qian to bind himself to Yuan Shao; about to go to Jing province, Qian again with Mi Zhu together were envoys to Liu Biao, all as finger and intention.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei broke with Cao Cao, he sent Sun Qian to open ties with Yuan Shao; later, as Liu prepared to move into Jing province, Sun Qian and Mi Zhu were dispatched together to Liu Biao, and every mission went exactly as Liu Bei wished.

sentences.zh: 后表與袁尚書，說其兄弟分爭之變，曰︰「每與劉左將軍、孫公佑共論此事，未嘗不痛心入骨，相為悲傷也。

translations.literal: Later Biao in a letter to Yuan Shang, narrating the change of his brothers' division and quarrel, said: "Whenever with General of the Left Liu, Sun Gongyou together discussed this matter, never did we not pain heart entering bone, mutually for each other grieve."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao later wrote to Yuan Shang describing how the Yuan brothers had torn one another apart, saying, "Whenever I discussed it with General of the Left Liu Bei and Sun Gongyou, our hearts ached to the marrow and we grieved for one another."

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " Thus he was esteemed seen like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard in which Sun Qian was held.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，乾自從事中郎為秉忠將軍，見禮次麋竺，與簡雍同等。

translations.literal: When the First Lord settled Yi province, Qian from administrative clerk on the staff became General Who Upholds Loyalty, seen in courtesy next after Mi Zhu, equal with Jian Yong.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei secured Yi province, Sun Qian was promoted from administrative clerk on the staff to general who upholds loyalty; in the order of favor he ranked just below Mi Zhu and on a par with Jian Yong.

sentences.zh: 頃之，卒。

translations.literal: In a short while, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 簡雍字憲和，涿郡人也。

translations.literal: Jian Yong, courtesy name Xianhe, was a man of Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yong, styled Xianhe, came from Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 少與先主有舊，隨從周旋。

translations.literal: In youth he had old ties with the First Lord, followed in turning and circling.
translations.idiomatic: He had known Liu Bei since youth and followed him through every turn of fortune.

sentences.zh: 先主至荊州，雍與麋竺、孫乾同爲從事中郎，常爲談客，往來使命。

translations.literal: When the First Lord arrived at Jing province, Yong with Mi Zhu, Sun Qian together were administrative clerks on the staff, often were talking guests, going and coming on missions.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei reached Jing province, Jian Yong served with Mi Zhu and Sun Qian as administrative clerks on the staff; he was often kept at court for counsel and sent back and forth on diplomatic errands.

sentences.zh: 先主入益州，劉璋見雍，甚愛之。

translations.literal: When the First Lord entered Yi province, Liu Zhang saw Yong, greatly loved him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei marched into Yi province, Liu Zhang met Jian Yong and took a great liking to him.

sentences.zh: 後先主圍成都，遣雍往說璋，璋遂與雍同輿而載，出城歸命。

translations.literal: Afterward when the First Lord besieged Chengdu, he sent Yong to persuade Zhang; Zhang then with Yong in the same carriage rode, left the city and submitted command.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Liu Bei besieged Chengdu, he sent Jian Yong to persuade Liu Zhang to yield. Liu Zhang then rode out of the city in the same carriage with Jian Yong and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 先主拜雍爲昭德將軍。

translations.literal: The First Lord invested Yong as General Who Illuminates Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei appointed him general who illuminates virtue.

sentences.zh: 優游風儀，性簡傲跌宕，在先主坐席，猶箕踞傾倚，威儀不肅，自縱適；

translations.literal: Leisurely roaming in bearing and deportment, by nature simple, proud, and unrestrained; in the First Lord's seating mat, still sat spread-legged leaning, awe-inspiring deportment not solemn, self-indulgent at ease;
translations.idiomatic: He carried himself with an easy grace but was by nature aloof and untrammeled: even in Liu Bei’s presence he would sprawl with legs outstretched or lounge against the cushions, careless of formal dignity and quite at his own ease;

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮已下則獨擅一榻，項枕卧語，無所爲屈。

translations.literal: From Zhuge Liang downward he alone monopolized one couch, neck-pillowed lying speaking, nothing made him bend.
translations.idiomatic: with everyone from Zhuge Liang downward he would hog a couch to himself, pillow his neck, and hold conversation reclining—nothing could make him defer.

sentences.zh: 時天旱禁酒，釀者有刑。

translations.literal: At the time heaven drought forbade wine; brewers had punishment.
translations.idiomatic: There was a drought at the time and wine was banned; anyone caught brewing faced punishment.

sentences.zh: 吏於人家索得釀具，論者欲令與作酒者同罰。

translations.literal: Clerks at people's homes searched and obtained brewing tools; those who judged wished to make them suffer the same punishment as wine-makers.
translations.idiomatic: Officials raided a household and found distilling equipment; some argued that the owners should be punished like actual brewers.

sentences.zh: 雍與先主游觀，見一男女行道，謂先主曰：「彼人欲行淫，何以不縛？

translations.literal: Yong with the First Lord strolling and viewing, saw one man and woman walking the road, said to the First Lord: "Those people wish to commit lewdness; why not bind them?
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yong was out walking with Liu Bei when he spotted a man and a woman on the road. He said to Liu Bei, "Those two mean to commit adultery—why do you not arrest them?

sentences.zh: 」先主曰：「卿何以知之？

translations.literal: " The First Lord said: "How do you know it?
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei asked, "How do you know that?

sentences.zh: 」雍對曰：「彼有其具，與欲釀者同。

translations.literal: " Yong replied: "They have its tools, the same as those who wish to brew.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian Yong answered, "They possess the means for the act, just like a man who keeps brewing gear when wine is forbidden."

sentences.zh: 」先主大笑，而原欲釀者。

translations.literal: " The First Lord greatly laughed, and pardoned those who wished to brew.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei burst out laughing and let the would-be brewers go.

sentences.zh: 雍之滑稽，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Yong's jesting, all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yong’s wit ran in this vein.

sentences.zh: 〈或曰：雍本姓耿，幽州人語謂耿爲簡，遂隨音變之。〉

translations.literal: Some say: Yong's original surname was Geng; Youzhou people's speech called Geng as Jian, therefore followed the sound and changed it."
translations.idiomatic: Some say his surname was originally Geng, which in the Youzhou dialect sounded like Jian, so the name shifted with local pronunciation."

sentences.zh: 伊籍字伯機，山陽人。

translations.literal: Yi Ji, courtesy name Boji, was a man of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ji, styled Boji, was a native of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 少依邑人鎮南將軍劉表。

translations.literal: In youth he relied on fellow townsman General Who Guards the South Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he took service under his townsman Liu Biao, general who guards the south.

sentences.zh: 先主之在荊州，籍常往來自托。

translations.literal: When the First Lord was in Jing province, Ji often went and came, self-entrusting.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Bei was in Jing province, Yi Ji made a point of calling on him and placing himself at Liu Bei’s disposal.

sentences.zh: 表卒，遂隨先主南渡江，從入益州。

translations.literal: When Biao died, then he followed the First Lord south crossing the river, followed entering Yi province.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Biao’s death he followed Liu Bei south across the Yangzi and accompanied him into Yi province.

sentences.zh: 益州既定，以籍為左將軍從事中郎，見待亞于簡雍、孫乾等。

translations.literal: When Yi province was already settled, he appointed Ji as administrative clerk on the staff to the General of the Left; in treatment seen he was next after Jian Yong, Sun Qian, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yi province was pacified, Liu Bei named him administrative clerk on the staff of the general of the left; in rank of favor he stood just below Jian Yong and Sun Qian.

sentences.zh: 遣東使于吳，孫權聞其才辨，欲逆折以辭。

translations.literal: Sent east as envoy to Wu; Sun Quan heard his talent in disputation, wished to meet and break him with words.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent east as envoy to Wu. Sun Quan, having heard of his eloquence, meant to trip him up with sharp questions.

sentences.zh: 籍適入拜，權曰︰「勞事無道之君乎？

translations.literal: Ji just entered and bowed; Quan said: "Do you toil serving a lord without the Way?
translations.idiomatic: As Yi Ji came in to pay his respects, Sun Quan said, "It must be exhausting to serve a worthless sovereign?

sentences.zh: 」籍即對曰︰「一拜一起，未足為勞。

translations.literal: " Ji immediately replied: "One bow one rise, not sufficient to count as toil.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi Ji shot back, "A single bow and straightening up hardly counts as hard work."

sentences.zh: 」籍之機捷，類皆如此，權甚異之。

translations.literal: " Ji's quick wit, in kind all like this; Quan greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: " His repartee was always as quick as this, and Sun Quan was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 后遷昭文將軍，與諸葛亮、法正、劉巴、李嚴共造《蜀科》；

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to General Who Illuminates Culture, with Zhuge Liang, Fa Zheng, Liu Ba, Li Yan together composed the Shu Code;
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to general who illuminates culture and, with Zhuge Liang, Fa Zheng, Liu Ba, and Li Yan, drafted the Shu legal code;

sentences.zh: 《蜀科》之製，由此五人焉。

translations.literal: the establishment of the Shu Code, from these five men.
translations.idiomatic: those five men were the authors of the code’s provisions.

sentences.zh: 秦宓字子敕，廣漢綿竹人也。

translations.literal: Qin Mi, courtesy name Zichi, was a man of Mianzhu in Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Mi, styled Zichi, was a native of Mianzhu in Guanghan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有才學，州郡辟命，輒稱疾不往。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent and learning; province and commandery summoned with appointments, he always claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted with literary talent from youth, he nevertheless pleaded illness whenever the province or commandery summoned him to office.

sentences.zh: 奏記州牧劉焉，荐儒士任定祖曰︰

translations.literal: He presented a memorial to the shepherd of the province Liu Yan, recommending the scholar Ren Dingzu, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial to provincial shepherd Liu Yan recommending the scholar Ren Dingzu in these words:

sentences.zh: 昔百里、蹇叔以耆艾而定策，甘羅、子奇以童冠而立功，故《書》美黃發，而《易》稱顏淵，固知選士用能，不拘長幼，明矣。

translations.literal: Formerly Baili and Jian Shu by old age fixed strategy; Gan Luo and Ziqi by youth cap established merit; therefore the Document praises yellow hair, and the Changes praises Yan Yuan; thus knowing selecting gentlemen and employing ability does not bind long and young, is clear.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Baili Xi and Jian Shu counseled states in their gray years, while Gan Luo and Ziqi won fame while still in their teens; the Shang shu praises white-haired elders and the Zhou yi celebrates Yan Yuan. Choosing men for office should never be shackled to age—that much is plain.

sentences.zh: 乃者以來，海內察舉，率多英俊而遺舊齒，眾論不齊，異同相伴，此乃承平之翔步，非亂世之急務也。

translations.literal: From recent times onward, within the seas investigation and recommendation, mostly many handsome youths and cast aside old teeth, crowd discussion not uniform, difference and sameness mutually accompany; this is the soaring step of great peace, not the urgent task of chaotic age.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, recommendations across the realm have favored bright young men while casting aside the aged; opinion is divided and voices contradict one another. That may suit an age of untroubled order, but it is no remedy for times in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 夫欲救危撫亂，修己以安人，則宜卓犖超倫，與時殊趣，震驚鄰國，駭動四方，上當天心，下合人意；

translations.literal: As for wishing to save peril and calm chaos, cultivate self to pacify others, then ought to be outstanding beyond the flock, with the times have different bent, shock neighboring states, startle move four quarters, above match Heaven's heart, below join human intent;
translations.idiomatic: To rescue a realm in danger and bring peace from chaos, to cultivate oneself and steady the people, you need men who tower above their peers and march out of step with vulgar fashion—men who can awe neighboring states and stir the four quarters, whose aims match Heaven above and the hopes of men below;

sentences.zh: 天人既和，內省不疚，雖遭凶亂，何憂何懼﹗昔楚葉公好龍，神龍下之，好偽徹天，何況于真？

translations.literal: Heaven and man already harmonious, inner examination without fault; although encountering fierce chaos, what worry what fear! Formerly Chu Duke Ye loved dragons, divine dragon descended to him; love of the false penetrated Heaven, how much more of the true?
translations.idiomatic: when Heaven and the human heart are at one and a man’s conscience is clear, what is there to fear though chaos rage about him? The Duke of Ye in Chu doted on dragons until a real dragon descended—if sham devotion can move Heaven, how much more will genuine worth do?

sentences.zh: 今處士任安，仁義直道，流名四遠；

translations.literal: Now the scholar-at-home Ren An, benevolence and righteousness straight way, flowing name to four distances;
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Ren An walks the straight path of benevolence and righteousness, and his name has traveled to the farthest corners of the land;

sentences.zh: 如今見察，則一州斯服。

translations.literal: if now he is seen and investigated, then one province thereby will submit.
translations.idiomatic: if you now call him to office, the whole province will gladly defer.

sentences.zh: 昔湯舉伊芳尹，不仁者遠，何武貢二龔，雙名竹帛，故貪尋常之高而忽萬仞之嵩，樂面前之飾而忘天下之譽，斯誠往古之所重慎也。

translations.literal: Formerly Tang raised Yi Yin, the unbenevolent were distant; He Wu presented the two Gongs, both names on bamboo and silk; therefore to covet ordinary height and neglect ten thousand ren's Song, delight in ornament before the face and forget the world's praise, this is truly what past antiquity valued and was cautious about.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang raised Yi Yin, the cruel drifted far away; when He Wu presented the two brothers Gong, both names were written into history. To chase petty reputation while ignoring a peak like Mount Song, or to delight in hollow show and forget the judgment of the world—that is the very mistake the sages of old warned against.

sentences.zh: 甫欲鑿石索玉，剖蚌求珠，今乃隨、和炳然，有如皎日，複何疑哉﹗誠知晝不操燭，日有余光，但愚情區區，貪陳所見。」

translations.literal: I just wished to chisel stone seeking jade, split clam seeking pearl; now then Sui and He shine bright, like the bright sun, what again doubt! Truly knowing daytime does not hold torch, sun has surplus light, only my foolish feeling petty petty, greedily set forth what I have seen."
translations.idiomatic: I meant only to chip stone in search of jade or split a shell for a pearl; here before you lies a jewel bright as the He family pearls in broad daylight—what room is left for doubt? I know broad daylight needs no candle and the sun still has light to spare; yet in my humble zeal I cannot help laying these thoughts before you."

sentences.zh: 〈益部耆舊傳曰：安，廣漢人。

translations.literal: The Yibu Qijiu Zhuan states: An was a man of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: The Traditions of the Elders of Yi records that Ren An was a native of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 少事聘士楊厚，究極圖籍，遊覽京師，還家講授，與董扶俱以學行齊聲。

translations.literal: In youth he served summoned gentleman Yang Hou, exhaustively reached charts and records, toured and viewed the capital, returned home lecturing and teaching, with Dong Fu together by learning and conduct equal sound.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under the summoned scholar Yang Hou, mastered the classical corpus, traveled to the capital, then returned home to teach; he and Dong Fu were equally famed for scholarship and conduct.

sentences.zh: 郡請功曹，州辟治中別駕，終不久居。

translations.literal: The commandery invited him as merit assessor; the province summoned him as administrative clerk or attendant clerk; in the end he did not long dwell.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery offered him the post of merit assessor and the province summoned him as administrative or attendant clerk, but he never stayed long in any appointment.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉茂才，太尉載辟，除博士，公車徵，皆稱疾不就。

translations.literal: Recommended filial and incorrupt and flourishing talent, the grand commandant repeatedly summoned, appointed erudite, summoned by public carriage, all claimed illness and did not take up.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended on the filial-and-incorrupt and flourishing-talent rolls; the grand commandant summoned him repeatedly; he was offered the post of erudite and summoned by imperial carriage—each time he pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 州牧劉焉表薦安味精道度，厲節高邈，揆其器量，國之元寶，宜處弼疑之輔，以消非常之咎。

translations.literal: Shepherd of the province Liu Yan in a memorial recommended An as embodying refined way measure, stern integrity high remote, measuring his vessel capacity, the state's primal treasure, ought to be placed as supporting-doubt assistant, thereby to eliminate extraordinary blame.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial shepherd Liu Yan memorialized that Ren An embodied the Way in his bearing, upheld the loftiest integrity, and possessed capacity fit for a cornerstone of the state—that he should be given a post at the ruler’s side to avert extraordinary misfortune.

sentences.zh: 玄纁之禮，所宜招命。

translations.literal: The rite of dark and light silks, what is fitting to summon and command.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man worthy of the silken summons of high office.

sentences.zh: 王塗隔塞，遂無聘命。

translations.literal: The royal path was blocked and cut off, therefore there was no summoning appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Because imperial authority no longer reached the region, the summons never came.

sentences.zh: 年七十九，建安七年卒，門人慕仰，為立碑銘。

translations.literal: Age seventy-nine, in the seventh year of Jian'an died; disciples admired and looked up, for him erected stele inscription.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jian’an 7 at the age of seventy-nine; his students, who revered him, set up a stele with an inscription in his memory.

sentences.zh: 後丞相亮問秦宓以安所長，宓曰：「記人之善，忘人之過。」〉

translations.literal: Later Chancellor Liang asked Qin Mi what An's strengths were; Mi said: "He remembered others' good, forgot others' faults."
translations.idiomatic: Later the chancellor Zhuge Liang asked Qin Mi what Ren An’s strengths had been. Qin Mi replied, "He remembered men’s virtues and forgot their faults."

sentences.zh: 劉璋時，宓同郡王商為治中從事，與宓書曰︰「貧賤困苦，亦何時可以終身﹗卞和炫玉以耀世，宜一來，與州尊相見。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time, Mi's fellow townsman Wang Shang was administrative clerk on the staff, in a letter to Mi said: "Poor and lowly bitter hardship, also when can one end life! Bian He displayed jade to dazzle the world; you ought once to come and meet the provincial venerable.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang, Wang Shang of Qin Mi’s commandery served as administrative clerk on the staff. He wrote to Qin Mi: "Poverty and obscurity are a grinding burden—how long can you endure them? Bian He showed his jade to dazzle the world; you should come once and meet the provincial chief."

sentences.zh: 」宓答書曰：

translations.literal: " Mi answered the letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Qin Mi replied:

sentences.zh: 昔堯優許由，非不弘也，洗其兩耳；

translations.literal: Formerly Yao treated Xu You generously; it was not that he was not magnanimous; Xu washed his two ears;
translations.idiomatic: Yao treated Xu You with the utmost generosity, yet Xu You washed his ears to cleanse them of the offer—Yao was not lacking in largesse;

sentences.zh: 楚聘莊周，非不廣也，執竿罔顧。

translations.literal: Chu hired Zhuang Zhou; it was not that it was not broad; he held the pole and did not look back.
translations.idiomatic: Chu’s invitation to Zhuang Zhou was magnificently generous, yet Zhuang Zhou stood with his fishing rod and never turned his head.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰‘確乎其不可拔’，夫何炫之有？

translations.literal: The Changes says 'firm indeed, it cannot be uprooted'; what dazzling is there?
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou yi says of the steadfast that they cannot be uprooted—where is the need for ostentation?

sentences.zh: 且以國君之賢，子為良輔，不以是時建蕭、張之策，未足為智也。

translations.literal: Moreover with the state lord's worthiness, you as good assistant, not at this time establishing Xiao and Zhang's strategies, is not sufficient to count as wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: You serve a worthy lord as his able aide; if you fail to advance policies like those of Xiao He and Zhang Liang at such a moment, I would not call that wisdom.

sentences.zh: 仆得曝背乎隴畝之中，誦顏氏之簞瓢，詠原憲之蓬戶，時翱翔于林澤，與沮、溺等儔，聽玄猿之悲吟，察鶴鳴于九皋，安身為樂，無憂為福，處空虛之名，居不靈之龜，知我者希，則我貴矣。

translations.literal: Your servant obtains to sun his back in the ridge fields, chant Yan's basket and gourd, sing Yuan Xian's brushwood door, at times soar in forests and marshes, with Ju and Ni as companions, listen to dark apes' sad chant, observe crane cry in the nine marshes, settling body as joy, no worry as blessing, dwell in empty void name, reside in non-spirit tortoise, those who know me are few, then I am noble.
translations.idiomatic: I prefer to warm my back in the furrows, chant of Yan Hui’s basket and ladle, dwell on Yuan Xian’s wattled gate, roam the woods and marshes with men like Chang Ju and Jie Ni, listen to the gibbons’ mournful cry and the cranes calling from the deep pools—to find peace in a quiet life, to count freedom from care as blessing, to wear an empty reputation and shelter under an unlucky tortoise shell. When few understand you, that itself is nobility.

sentences.zh: 斯乃仆得志之秋也，何困苦之戚焉﹗」后商為嚴君平、李弘立祠，宓與書曰︰「疾病伏匿，甫知足下為嚴、李立祠，可謂濃黨勤類者也。

translations.literal: This is then your servant's obtaining-will autumn; what bitter hardship's sorrow!" Later Shang for Yan Junping, Li Hong erected shrines; Mi in a letter said: "Illness lying hidden, just then learned you for Yan, Li erected shrines, can be called thick party diligent in kind.
translations.idiomatic: That is the season of my heart’s content—what misery is there in poverty?" Later Wang Shang founded shrines for Yan Junping and Li Hong. Qin Mi wrote to him: "I have been ill and in seclusion; only now do I learn that you have raised shrines to Yan and Li—you are indeed zealous in honoring your own kind."

sentences.zh: 觀嚴文章，冠冒天下，由、夷逸操，山岳不移，使揚子不嘆，固自昭明。

translations.literal: Observing Yan's writings, cap-crown over the world, You and Yi's reclusive conduct, mountains and peaks not moving, had Yangzi not sighed, would of itself be bright clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Junping’s writings crown the realm; his reclusive integrity rivals that of Xu You and Bo Yi—firm as a mountain. Even without Yang Xiong’s praise he would shine by his own light.

sentences.zh: 如李仲元不遭《法言》，令名必淪，其無虎豹之文故也，可謂攀龍附鳳者矣。

translations.literal: As for Li Zhongyuan, had he not encountered the Expository Words, his fair name would surely have sunk; because he lacked tiger leopard patterns, can be called climbing dragon attaching phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Had Li Zhongyuan not been noticed in Yang Xiong’s Fa yan, his good name would have sunk in oblivion, for he lacked the striking markings of tiger or leopard—one might say he rose by clinging to dragon and phoenix.

sentences.zh: 如揚子雲潛心著述，有補于世，泥幡不滓，行參聖師，于今海內，談詠厥辭。

translations.literal: As for Yang Ziyun, sinking heart in writing and composing, having supplement for the world, mud banner not stained, conduct joined sage teacher; within the seas today, they discuss and chant his phrases.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong devoted himself to writing that benefited the world; though he rode in a plain cart his conduct ranked with the sages, and to this day scholars across the land recite his words.

sentences.zh: 邦有斯人，以耀四遠，怪子替茲，不立祠堂。

translations.literal: The state having this man, thereby dazzles four distances; I marvel that you, replacing this, do not erect a shrine hall.
translations.idiomatic: A state that possesses such a man sends his light to the four quarters; I am surprised you neglect him and raise no shrine.

sentences.zh: 蜀本無學士，文翁遣相如東受七經，還教吏民，于是蜀學比于齊、魯。

translations.literal: Shu originally had no scholars; Wen Weng sent Xiangru east to receive the seven classics, returned to teach clerks and people; thereby Shu learning compared with Qi and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu once had no learned tradition until Wen Weng sent Sima Xiangru east to master the seven classics and brought him back to instruct officials and commoners; only then did learning in Shu rival that of Qi and Lu.

sentences.zh: 故《地裡志》曰︰‘文翁倡其教，相如為之師。

translations.literal: Therefore the Treatise on Geography says: 'Wen Weng initiated its teaching, Xiangru was its teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Geography therefore says, ‘Wen Weng began the teaching, and Sima Xiangru became its master.’

sentences.zh: ’漢家得士，盛于其世；

translations.literal: ' The Han house obtaining gentlemen, flourished in that age;
translations.idiomatic: The Han found its finest talent in that very generation;

sentences.zh: 仲舒之徒，不達封禪，相如製其禮。

translations.literal: Zhongshu and his kind, did not comprehend feng and shan; Xiangru made their rites.
translations.idiomatic: men like Dong Zhongshu did not grasp the feng and shan sacrifices, but Sima Xiangru drafted their ritual.

sentences.zh: 夫能製禮造樂，移風易俗，非禮所秩有益于世者乎﹗雖有王孫之累，猶孔子大齊桓之霸，公羊賢叔術之讓。

translations.literal: As for one able to make rites and create music, shift wind and change customs, is this not what rites order ranks as beneficial to the world! Although there is Wangsun's encumbrance, still Confucius magnified Qi Huan's hegemony, the Gongyang esteems Shushu's yielding.
translations.idiomatic: To frame ritual and compose music, to shift customs and improve the age—is that not the greatest service rites can render the world? Though Sima Xiangru bore the burden of his connection to Zhuo Wangsun, Confucius still praised Duke Huan of Qi for his hegemony, and the Gongyang zhuan honors Shushu of Lu for yielding his claim.

sentences.zh: 仆亦善長卿之化，宜立祠堂，速定其銘。

translations.literal: Your servant also esteems Changqing's transformation; ought to erect shrine hall, quickly fix its inscription.
translations.idiomatic: I too admire the transformation Sima Xiangru worked in this land; you should raise a shrine for him at once and set the inscription without delay."

sentences.zh: 先是，李權從宓借《戰國策》，宓曰︰「戰國從橫，用之何為？

translations.literal: Before this, Li Quan from Mi borrowed the Intrigues of the Warring States; Mi said: "Warring States vertical and horizontal, using them for what?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Quan had asked to borrow Qin Mi’s copy of the Intrigues of the Warring States. Qin Mi said, "Those are the arts of alliance and defection—what would you do with them?

sentences.zh: 」權曰︰「仲尼、嚴平，會聚眾書，以成《春秋》、《指歸》之文，故海以合流為大，君子以博識為弘。

translations.literal: " Quan said: "Zhongni, Yan Ping, gathered many books, thereby to complete the Spring and Autumn, Pointing Home texts; therefore the sea takes joining streams as great, the gentleman takes broad knowledge as vast.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Quan replied, "Confucius and Yan Junping brought together many books to compose the Chunqiu and the Zhigui—just as the sea is great because all rivers flow into it, so the gentleman is great through wide learning."

sentences.zh: 」宓報曰︰

translations.literal: " Mi replied saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Qin Mi answered:

sentences.zh: 書非史記周圖，仲尼不采，道非虛無自然，嚴平不演。

translations.literal: Books that are not the historical records of Zhou charts, Zhongni did not gather; the Way that is not empty void self-so, Yan Ping did not expound.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius took nothing into the classics that was not grounded in the histories and charts of Zhou; Yan Junping expounded no Way that was not rooted in emptiness and naturalness.

sentences.zh: 海以受淤，歲一蕩清；

translations.literal: The sea by receiving silt, each year once washes clear;
translations.idiomatic: The sea accepts silt from every stream, yet each year a great tide scours it clean;

sentences.zh: 君子博識，非禮不視。

translations.literal: the gentleman's broad knowledge, if not ritual he does not view.
translations.idiomatic: and the gentleman may read widely, but he does not look at what is contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 今戰國反覆儀、秦之術，殺人自生，亡人自存，經之所疾。

translations.literal: Now the Warring States turn and return the arts of Yi and Qin, kill others to live oneself, destroy others to preserve oneself; the classics abhor this.
translations.idiomatic: The Intrigues teach the shifting schemes of Su Qin and Zhang Yi—killing others to save oneself, ruining others to survive. The classics condemn such things.

sentences.zh: 故孔子發憤作《春秋》。

translations.literal: Therefore Kongzi in wrath composed the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Confucius, in indignation, composed the Chunqiu.

sentences.zh: 大乎居正，複製《孝經》，廣陳德行。

translations.literal: Great is dwelling in rectitude; again he made the Classic of Filial Piety, broadly set forth virtue and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: How great is the principle of holding to the right! He also composed the Classic of Filial Piety to set forth virtue in breadth.

sentences.zh: 杜漸防萌，預有所抑，是以老氏絕禍于未萌，豈不信邪﹗成湯大聖，睹野魚而有獵逐之失，定公賢者，見女樂而棄朝事，

translations.literal: Stop gradual prevent sprouting, beforehand have what to restrain; therefore the Old Master cut off disaster before not sprouting, is it not trustworthy! Cheng Tang great sage, seeing wild fish yet had hunting pursuit's fault; Duke Ding worthy man, seeing women's music then abandoned court affairs,
translations.idiomatic: He checked evil in its first stirrings and curbed excess before it could grow—hence Laozi cuts off calamity before it buds; can you doubt it? Tang the Completer was a great sage, yet the sight of wild game led him to hunting excess; Duke Ding of Lu was a worthy ruler, yet the sight of female musicians made him neglect court business;

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：書傳魯定公無善可稱。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi investigates: in documents and transmissions Duke Ding of Lu has no good worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: the transmitted texts record no virtue in Duke Ding of Lu worth praising.

sentences.zh: 宓謂之賢者，淺學所未達也。〉

translations.literal: Mi calling him worthy man, shallow learning has not reached."
translations.idiomatic: For Qin Mi to call him a worthy shows a shallow reading of the sources."

sentences.zh: 若此輩類，焉可勝陳。

translations.literal: If this sort of kind, how can they be fully arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Examples of this sort could fill many pages.

sentences.zh: 道家法曰︰‘不見所欲，使心不亂。

translations.literal: The Daoist law says: 'Not seeing what is desired, causes the mind not to be chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist maxim runs, ‘Give the eye no craving and the heart will not be thrown into turmoil.’

sentences.zh: ’是故天地貞觀，日月貞明，其直如矢，君子所覆。

translations.literal: ' Therefore Heaven and Earth are correct in viewing, sun and moon correct in brightness; their straightness like arrows; what the gentleman covers.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Heaven and Earth hold to constancy, sun and moon shine with constancy, and the straight course flies like an arrow—such is the model the gentleman embraces."

sentences.zh: 《洪范》記災，發于言貌，何戰國之譎權乎哉﹗

translations.literal: The Hong Fan records disasters, arising from speech and appearance; what Warring States deceitful stratagems!
translations.idiomatic: The Hong fan traces calamity to words and bearing—what have they to do with the cunning stratagems of the Warring States?

sentences.zh: 或謂宓曰︰「足下欲自比于巢、許、四皓，何故揚文藻見瑰穎乎？

translations.literal: Someone said to Mi: "You wish to compare yourself to Chao, Xu, the Four Hoaryheads; why then display literary ornament and show rare brilliance?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Qin Mi, "You style yourself after Nest Father, Xu You, and the Four Hoaryheads of Shang—why then parade literary ornament and show off your brilliance?

sentences.zh: 」宓答曰︰「仆文不能盡言，言不能盡意，何文藻之有揚乎﹗昔孔子三見哀公，言成七卷，事蓋有不可嘿嘿也。

translations.literal: " Mi answered: "Your servant's writing cannot exhaust speech, speech cannot exhaust meaning; what literary ornament is there to display! Formerly Kongzi three times saw Duke Ai of Lu, speech became seven scrolls; matters probably have what cannot be darkly silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Qin Mi replied, "My writing cannot exhaust my words, nor my words my meaning—where is the ornament? Confucius met Duke Ai of Lu three times and left seven scrolls of discourse; some truths cannot be left unspoken."

sentences.zh: 〈劉向《七略》曰：孔子三見哀公，作三朝記七篇，今在大戴禮。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's Seven Summaries states: Kongzi three times saw Duke Ai, made Three Court Records in seven pieces; now they are in the Da Dai Li.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang’s Qi lue states that after three audiences with Duke Ai, Confucius composed the San chao ji in seven sections, now preserved in the Da Dai li.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：中經部有孔子三朝八卷，一卷目錄，餘者所謂七篇。〉

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi investigates: in the Zhongjing section there is Kongzi's Three Courts in eight scrolls, one scroll catalogue; the remainder is what is called the seven pieces."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: the Zhong jing catalogue lists Kongzi’s San chao ji in eight fascicles, one of which is a table of contents, leaving the seven sections mentioned above."

sentences.zh: 接輿行且歌，論家以光篇；

translations.literal: Jie Yu walked and sang; discussers of doctrine thereby brightened their chapters;
translations.idiomatic: Jie Yu walked along singing, and scholars cite his words to lend luster to their own essays;

sentences.zh: 漁父詠滄浪，賢者以耀章。

translations.literal: The Fisherman chanted the dark waves; worthies thereby to dazzle their compositions.
translations.idiomatic: the Fisherman chanted of the Canglang waters, and the wise quote him to burnish their writings.

sentences.zh: 此二人者，非有欲于時者也。

translations.literal: These two men were not ones who had desire toward the age.
translations.idiomatic: Neither of these two courted the favor of his times.

sentences.zh: 夫虎生而文??，鳳生而五色，豈以五采自飾畫哉？

translations.literal: As for the tiger, born then patterns??; the phoenix, born then five colors—how could it be that by five colors they self-adorn and paint?
translations.idiomatic: The tiger is born with its stripes, the phoenix with its five hues—do you think they painted themselves with pigments?

sentences.zh: 天性自然也。

translations.literal: Heaven-nature is self-so.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply their inborn nature.

sentences.zh: 蓋《河》、《洛》由文興，六經由文起，君子懿文德，采藻其何傷﹗以仆之愚，猶恥革子成之誤，況賢于己者乎﹗」

translations.literal: In general the River Diagram and Luo Document rose through pattern; the six classics rose through pattern; the gentleman beautifies pattern-virtue—what harm in gathering water-plants! With your servant's stupidity, still ashamed at Ge Zicheng's error, how much more one worthy beyond oneself!"
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River chart and Luo River writing came forth through culture; the six classics arose from the written word; the gentleman ennobles his moral power in letters—what injury is there in literary polish? In my dullness I still blush for Ji Zicheng’s mistake—how much more should a man wiser than myself!"

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：今論語作棘子成。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi investigates: in today's Analects it is written Ji Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: the received Analects reads Ji Zicheng here.

sentences.zh: 子成曰：「君子質而已矣，何以文為！

translations.literal: Zicheng said: "The gentleman is substance only; what use is pattern!
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng said, "The gentleman needs only native substance—of what use is refinement?!"

sentences.zh: 」屈於子貢之言，故謂之誤也。〉

translations.literal: " He yielded to Zigong's words; therefore it is called an error."
translations.idiomatic: " He was refuted by Zigong, so I call his remark a mistake."

sentences.zh: 先主既定益州，廣漢太守夏侯纂請宓為師友祭酒，領五官掾，稱曰仲父。

translations.literal: When the First Lord had already settled Yi province, Grand Warden of Guanghan Xiahou Zuan requested Mi as libationer for teachers and friends, concurrently heading the clerk of the five bureaus, called him Second Father.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei secured Yi province, Xiahou Zuan, grand warden of Guanghan, invited Qin Mi to serve as libationer for teachers and friends and concurrently as clerk of the five bureaus, addressing him as "uncle" in the manner of Guan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 宓稱疾，臥在第舍，纂將功曹古朴，主簿王普，廚膳即宓第宴談，宓臥如故。

translations.literal: Mi claimed illness, lay in his residence; Zuan led merit assessor Gu Pu, chief clerk Wang Pu, kitchen provisions to Mi's residence for banquet talk; Mi lay as before.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Mi pleaded illness and stayed in bed at home. Xiahou Zuan brought his merit assessor Gu Pu, his chief clerk Wang Pu, and a full kitchen staff to Qin Mi’s house for a banquet and conversation, but Qin Mi remained stretched out as before.

sentences.zh: 纂問朴曰︰「至於貴州養生之具，實絕餘州矣，不知士人何如餘州也？

translations.literal: Zuan asked Pu saying: "As for your honorable state's tools for nurturing life, they truly surpass the remaining states; I do not know how scholars compare to the remaining states?
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Zuan asked Gu Pu, "Your province’s means of sustaining life are plainly richer than elsewhere—but how do its gentlemen compare with those of other regions?

sentences.zh: 」朴對曰︰「乃自先漢以來，其爵位者或不如餘州耳，至於著作為世師式，不負于餘州也。

translations.literal: " Pu replied: "From Former Han onward, as for those with rank and position perhaps they do not match the other states only; as for writings that become models for the age, they do not fall short of the other states.
translations.idiomatic: " Gu Pu replied, "Since Former Han, our men in high rank may not always have matched other regions, but for authors whose works became models for the world, we have nothing to apologize for beside any other province."

sentences.zh: 嚴君平見黃、老作《指歸》，揚雄見《易》作《太言》，見《論語》作《法言》，司馬相如主武帝製封禪之文，于今天下所共聞也。

translations.literal: Yan Junping encountered Huang and Lao and made Zhigui; Yang Xiong encountered the Changes and made Taixuan, encountered the Analects and made Expository Words; Sima Xiangru for Emperor Wu made feng and shan texts; as for today all under Heaven jointly have heard.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Junping expounded Huang-Lao thought in the Zhigui; Yang Xiong wrote the Taixuan jing from the Zhou yi and the Fa yan from the Analects; Sima Xiangru drafted the fengshan memorials for Emperor Wu—these names resound through the empire today."

sentences.zh: 」纂曰︰「仲父何如？

translations.literal: " Zuan said: "How about the Second Father?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiahou Zuan asked, "And what of your ‘uncle’ here?"
