sentences.zh: 」宓以簿擊頰，

translations.literal: " Mi with the tablet struck his cheek,
translations.idiomatic: " Qin Mi tapped his cheek with his writing tablet—

sentences.zh: 〈簿，手版也。〉

translations.literal: The tablet is the hand board.
translations.idiomatic: A "tablet" here means the wooden hand-board officials carried.

sentences.zh: 曰︰

translations.literal: He said:
translations.idiomatic: He spoke thus:

sentences.zh: 愿明府勿以仲父之言假于小草，民請為明府陳其本紀。

translations.literal: I wish the enlightened prefect not to take the Second Father's words and lend them to petty grass; your people request to for the enlightened prefect set forth its basic annals.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, my lord, not to weigh the praise you heard of your ‘uncle’ against this humble weed; allow your servant to lay before you the true pedigree of this land.

sentences.zh: 蜀有汶阜之山，江出其腹，帝以會昌，神以建福，故能沃野千里。

translations.literal: Shu has Mount Wenfu; the Yang emerges from its belly; the Di thereby meets flourishing, the spirits thereby establish blessing; therefore able fertile fields a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Shu holds the Wenfu range, from whose flank the Yangzi springs; there thearchs have gathered auspicious power and the gods founded blessing, which is why a thousand li of rich bottomland spread below.

sentences.zh: 〈《河图括地象》曰：岷山之地，上为东井络，帝以会昌，神以建福，上为天井。

translations.literal: The Hetu Kuodi Xiang states: The land of Mount Min, above is the net of Eastern Well; the Di thereby meets flourishing, the spirits thereby establish blessing; above is the Well of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Hetu kuodi xiang says the Min Mountains are girded aloft by the asterism Eastern Well, where thearchs gather splendor and the gods lay blessing, forming the celestial "well" above.

sentences.zh: 左思蜀都赋曰：远则岷山之精，上为井络，天地运期而会昌，景福

translations.literal: Zuo Si's Shu Capital Rhapsody says: In the distance then the essence of Mount Min, above forms the Well net; Heaven and Earth revolve their period and meet flourishing, bright blessing
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Si’s Rhapsody on the Shu capital says that far off the spirit of Mount Min rises as the Well constellation, that Heaven and Earth turn in their cycles to meet prosperity, and that bright blessing

translations.literal: (xi)
translations.idiomatic: rises in spreading fragrance (xi)

sentences.zh: 蚃而兴作。〉

translations.literal: fragrance and rises and arises."
translations.idiomatic: and takes shape there."

sentences.zh: 淮、濟四瀆，江為其首，此其一也。

translations.literal: Huai, Ji, the four channels; the Yang is their head; this is the first of them.
translations.idiomatic: Among Huai, Ji, and the four great rivers, the Yangzi is chief—this is the first point.

sentences.zh: 禹生石紐，今之汶山郡是也。

translations.literal: Yu was born at Stone Knot; this is today's Wenshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was born at Stone Knot, which is the present Wenshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《帝王世紀》曰：鯀納有莘氏女曰志，是為脩己。

translations.literal: The Diwang Shiji states: Gun took a woman of the Youxin clan named Zhi; this is Xiuji.
translations.idiomatic: The Diwang shiji says Gun married a woman of Youxin named Zhi, called Xiuji.

sentences.zh: 上山行，見流星貫昴，夢接意感，又吞神珠，臆圮胸折，而生禹於石紐。

translations.literal: Going up the mountain walking, she saw a shooting star pierce Mao; dream received intent moved; also swallowed a divine pearl; breast wall broken chest bent; and bore Yu at Stone Knot.
translations.idiomatic: Climbing a mountain she saw a meteor pierce the Mao asterism; the vision entered her dreams and stirred her heart, and she swallowed a divine pearl until her breast seemed to break—and so she bore Yu at Stone Knot.

sentences.zh: 譙周《蜀本紀》曰：禹本汶山廣柔縣人也，生於石紐，其地名刳兒坪，見《世帝紀》。〉

translations.literal: Qiao Zhou's Shu Basic Annals states: Yu was originally a man of Guangrou county in Wenshan, born at Stone Knot; its place name is Ku'er Slope; see the Shidi Ji."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou’s Shu ben ji records that Yu was a native of Guangrou in Wenshan, born at a place called Ku’er Slope on Stone Knot—see the Shidi ji."

sentences.zh: 昔堯遭洪水，鯀所不治，禹疏江決河，東注于海，為民徐害，生民已來功莫先者，此其二也。

translations.literal: Formerly Yao encountered the great flood, which Gun could not govern; Yu dredged the Yang and opened the rivers, eastward poured into the sea, for the people slowly removed harm; since the birth of the people no merit has been prior; this is the second of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao faced the flood that Gun could not master, Yu dredged the rivers and cut channels eastward to the sea, lifting the scourge from the people—no deed since the birth of mankind has surpassed his; that is the second point.

sentences.zh: 天帝布治房心，決政參伐，參伐則益州分野，三皇乘祗車出谷口，今之斜谷是也。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Emperor spreads governance in Fang and Xin, decides government in Shen and Fa; Shen and Fa then is Yi province's field division; the Three August Ones rode the spirit cart out the valley mouth; this is today's Xie Valley.
translations.idiomatic: High Heaven set governance in the lodges Fang and Xin and fixed policy in Shen and Fa—the very field division of Yi province. The Three Sovereigns drove their sacred chariot out through the valley mouth, which is the present Xie Valley pass.

sentences.zh: 〈蜀記曰：三皇乘祗車出谷口。

translations.literal: The Shu Ji states: The Three August Ones rode the spirit cart out the valley mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ji records that the Three Sovereigns drove the sacred chariot out through the valley mouth.

sentences.zh: 未詳宓所由知為斜谷也。〉

translations.literal: It is not detailed by what Mi knew it was Xie Valley."
translations.idiomatic: It is unclear how Qin Mi identified that passage with Xie Valley."

sentences.zh: 此便鄙州之阡陌，明府以雅意論之，何若于天下乎？

translations.literal: This then is my humble state's paths and fields; the enlightened prefect with elegant intent discusses it—how does it compare within all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: These are the lanes and fields of our humble province: weigh them, my lord, with your cultivated judgment—how do they stand against the realm at large?

sentences.zh: 于是纂逡巡無以複答。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zuan hesitated and drew back, having nothing again to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Zuan drew back in embarrassment and could find no reply.

sentences.zh: 益州辟宓為從事祭酒。

translations.literal: Yi province summoned Mi as clerk libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Yi province summoned Qin Mi to serve as libationer for clerks on the staff.

sentences.zh: 先主既稱尊號，將東征吳，宓陳天時必無其利，坐下獄幽閉，然後貸出。

translations.literal: When the First Lord had already assumed the honored title, about to east campaign against Wu, Mi set forth that Heaven's season surely had no benefit for it; for this he sat and entered prison, secluded and shut; afterward was lent out.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei took the imperial title and prepared to march east against Wu, Qin Mi argued that the astrological signs forbade success; for that he was thrown into prison, but was later pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 建興二年，丞相亮領益州牧，選宓迎為別駕，尋拜左中郎將、長水校尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianxing, Chancellor Liang concurrently held shepherd of Yi province, selected Mi and welcomed him as attendant clerk; soon invested General of the Left Gentlemen of the Household, Colonel of Changshui.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 2, while Zhuge Liang held the concurrent post of shepherd of Yi province, he chose Qin Mi as attendant clerk, then soon appointed him general of the household gentlemen of the left and colonel of Changshui.

sentences.zh: 吳遣使張溫來聘，百官皆往餞焉。

translations.literal: Wu sent envoy Zhang Wen to visit on friendly mission; the hundred officials all went to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu sent Zhang Wen on a goodwill mission, the whole court turned out to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 眾人皆集而宓未往，亮累遣使促之，溫曰︰「彼何人也？

translations.literal: The crowd all gathered but Mi had not yet gone; Liang repeatedly sent envoys to urge him; Wen said: "What sort of man is that?
translations.idiomatic: Everyone assembled except Qin Mi. Zhuge Liang sent messenger after messenger to fetch him. Zhang Wen asked, "Who is he?

sentences.zh: 」亮曰︰「益州學士也。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "A scholar of Yi province.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuge Liang replied, "One of Yi province’s leading scholars."

sentences.zh: 」及至，溫問曰︰「君學乎？

translations.literal: " When he arrived, Wen asked saying: "Do you study?
translations.idiomatic: " When Qin Mi arrived, Zhang Wen asked, "Do you pursue learning?

sentences.zh: 」宓曰︰「五尺童子皆學，何必小人﹗」溫複問曰︰「天有頭乎？

translations.literal: " Mi said: "Five-foot children all study; how must it be petty men!" Wen again asked saying: "Does Heaven have a head?
translations.idiomatic: " Qin Mi said, "Even boys five feet tall are at their books—need you ask a mere nobody like me?" Zhang Wen pressed on: "Does Heaven have a head?

sentences.zh: 」宓曰︰「有之。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "It has one.
translations.idiomatic: " "It does."

sentences.zh: 」溫曰︰「在何方也？

translations.literal: " Wen said: "In what direction is it?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen asked, "In which direction does it lie?"

sentences.zh: 」宓曰︰「在西方。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "In the west.
translations.idiomatic: " "In the west."

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰︰『乃眷西顧。

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'Then he looked west with care.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says, ‘Then he turned his kindly gaze westward.’

sentences.zh: 』以此推之，頭在西方。

translations.literal: ' By this infer it; the head is in the west.
translations.idiomatic: From that line we infer that Heaven’s head lies in the west."

sentences.zh: 」溫曰︰「天有耳乎？

translations.literal: " Wen said: "Does Heaven have ears?
translations.idiomatic: " "Does Heaven have ears?"

sentences.zh: 」宓曰︰「天處高而聽卑，《詩》雲︰『鶴鳴于九皋，聲聞于天。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "Heaven dwells high yet listens low; the Odes says: 'The crane cries in the nine marshes; its voice is heard in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " "Heaven sits on high yet hears what is below, as the Poetry says: ‘The crane cries from the ninefold marsh; its voice reaches Heaven.’"

sentences.zh: 』若其無耳，何以聽之？

translations.literal: ' If it had no ears, how would it hear them?
translations.idiomatic: If it had no ears, how could it hear?"

sentences.zh: 」溫曰︰「天有足乎？

translations.literal: " Wen said: "Does Heaven have feet?
translations.idiomatic: " "Does Heaven have feet?"

sentences.zh: 」宓曰︰「有。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "It has.
translations.idiomatic: " "It does."

sentences.zh: 《詩》雲︰『天步艱難，之子不猶。

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'Heaven's steps are hard and steep; this man is not like others.
translations.idiomatic: The Poetry says, ‘Heaven’s march is steep and hard; this man is not like the others.’"

sentences.zh: 』若其無足，何以步之？

translations.literal: ' If it had no feet, how would it step them?
translations.idiomatic: If it had no feet, how could it walk?"

sentences.zh: 」溫曰︰「天有姓乎？

translations.literal: " Wen said: "Does Heaven have a surname?
translations.idiomatic: " "Does Heaven have a surname?"

sentences.zh: 」宓曰︰「有。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "It has.
translations.idiomatic: " "It does."

sentences.zh: 」溫曰︰「何姓？

translations.literal: " Wen said: "What surname?
translations.idiomatic: " "What surname?"

sentences.zh: 」宓曰︰「姓劉。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "Surnamed Liu.
translations.idiomatic: " "The surname Liu."

sentences.zh: 」溫曰︰「何以知之？

translations.literal: " Wen said: "How do you know it?
translations.idiomatic: " "How do you know?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰︰「天子姓劉，故以此知之。

translations.literal: " He answered saying: "The Son of Heaven is surnamed Liu; therefore by this I know it.
translations.idiomatic: " "The Son of Heaven is surnamed Liu—that is how I know."

sentences.zh: 」溫曰︰「日生于東乎？

translations.literal: " Wen said: "Is the sun born in the east?
translations.idiomatic: " "Is the sun born in the east?"

sentences.zh: 」宓曰︰「雖生于東而沒于西。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "Although born in the east, it sets in the west.
translations.idiomatic: " "It rises in the east but sets in the west."

sentences.zh: 」答問如響，應聲而出，于是溫大敬服。

translations.literal: " Answers and questions like echo, responding to sound and emerging; thereupon Wen greatly respected and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Each answer came back like an echo; Zhang Wen was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 宓之文辯，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Mi's literary disputation, all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Mi’s literary fencing was always of this order.

sentences.zh: 遷大司農，四年卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand minister of agriculture; in the fourth year died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand minister of agriculture and died in the fourth year of his tenure.

sentences.zh: 初宓見帝系之文，五帝皆同一族，宓辨其不然之本。

translations.literal: At first when Mi saw the text of the Imperial Genealogies, the Five Di were all of one clan; Mi distinguished that this was not so at root.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, reading the imperial genealogies that made the Five Thearchs one clan, Qin Mi argued the fundamental reasons why that could not be so.

sentences.zh: 又論皇帝王霸

translations.literal: Further he discussed the Thearch, Emperor, King, and Hegemon
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote on the thearch, emperor, king, and hegemon

translations.idiomatic: and the raising

sentences.zh: [豢]龍之說，甚有道理，譙允南少時數往咨訪，紀錄其言于《春秋然否論》，文多故不載。

translations.literal: the theory of raising dragons, very had the pattern of reason; Qiao Yunnan in youth several times went to consult and visit, recorded his words in the Discourse on Spring and Autumn Yes and No; the text being much, therefore is not carried.
translations.idiomatic: of the dragon-herding legend—arguments of real force. In his youth Qiao Zhou often went to consult him and set down his teachings in the Chunqiu ranyou lun; the text is too long to quote here.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Editorial appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰︰許靖夙有名節，既以篤濃為稱，又以人物為意，雖行事舉動，未悉允當，蔣濟以為「大較廊廟器」也。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Xu Jing from early had name and integrity; both by thick earnestness was praised, and by judging men was minded; although deeds and movements were not all fitting and proper, Jiang Ji considered him "in the main a hall-and-temple vessel."
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Xu Jing long enjoyed a reputation for integrity; he was celebrated for deep human warmth and for his eye for men. Not every choice he made was felicitous, yet Jiang Ji rightly called him, in the main, timber fit for the state’s high halls.

sentences.zh: 〈《萬機論》論許子將曰：許文休者，大較廊廟器也，而子將貶之。

translations.literal: The Wan Ji Lun discussing Xu Zijiang says: Xu Wenxiu is, in the main, a hall-and-temple vessel, yet Zijiang belittled him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wan ji lun, discussing Xu Shao, says Xu Wenxiu was essentially material for the imperial court, yet Xu Shao underrated him.

sentences.zh: 若實不貴之，是不明也；

translations.literal: If in truth he did not esteem him, this is not clarity;
translations.idiomatic: If he truly failed to value him, that showed poor judgment;

sentences.zh: 誠令知之，蓋善人也。〉

translations.literal: if sincerely let him know him, then he was a good man."
translations.idiomatic: if he did recognize his worth, then Xu Shao was a fair judge after all."

sentences.zh: 麋竺、孫乾、簡雍、伊藉，皆雍容風議，見禮于世。

translations.literal: Mi Zhu, Sun Qian, Jian Yong, Yi Ji, all were easy and grand in manner and discussion, seen in courtesy in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Zhu, Sun Qian, Jian Yong, and Yi Ji carried themselves with unhurried grace and were honored wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 秦宓始慕肥遁之高，而無若愚之實。

translations.literal: Qin Mi at first admired the height of fat reclusion, but lacked the substance of seeming foolishness.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Mi began by admiring the lofty reclusion of the hermit’s life, yet he never quite matched the substance of ‘wise folly.’

sentences.zh: 然專對有余，文藻壯美，可謂一時之才士矣。

translations.literal: Yet in exclusive reply he had surplus; literary ornament stately and beautiful; can be called a talented gentleman of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Still, he had more than enough wit for debate, and his prose was rich and strong—among the literary talents of his day he stood without peer.
